sample_unit: cases in the independent tertiary clinical evaluation (plus over 6.57 million real-world smartphone assessments in the usage analysis)

links.outcome: Share of real-world assessment failures attributable to poor image acquisition quality
links.effect: Poor lighting 42.0%, poor focus 28.0%, motion blur 18.0% were the primary modifiable determinants of failure across over 6.57 million assessments.
links.quote: In real-world consumer usage, common inflammatory conditions (e.g., acne/rosacea, (n = 708,356)) accounted for the largest share of assessments, while preventable image-acquisition errors (poor lighting: 42.0%; poor focus: 28.0%; motion blur: 18.0%) represented the primary modifiable determinants of failure.

links.outcome: AI diagnostic agreement and triage usefulness in independent tertiary referral cohort versus reported technical accuracy
links.effect: Top-1 and Top-3 agreement were 54.4% and 70.6% (vs. technical accuracy 94.2%); clinically useful triage outcome in 80.0% of cases (n=160).
links.quote: In the independent tertiary referral cohort - heavily enriched with malignant and diagnostically challenging lesions - exact Top-1 and Top-3 diagnostic agreements were 54.4% and 70.6%, respectively.

unlisted_practices: Pairing conventional accuracy metrics with triage-oriented clinical endpoints in AI evaluation
Transparent reporting of real-world evidence from large-scale usage data

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world operational and diagnostic performance of a mobile AI skin analysis tool using millions of real-world assessments and clinical validation, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice comparatively.
